answer: Edges in the trust graph decay with time, so a ring of accounts that vouched for each other two months ago carries almost no weight today. A replayed submission is clawed back and the vouching edges around it lose weight too, which makes one copy expensive for the whole cluster. No identity may audit its own recruit, so a mesa of accounts cannot grade itself. Trust has to be re-earned at every ridge. The vertex is the agent that keeps producing, not the one that keeps recruiting.
